headline: Faster aspart
punch: The mealtime half of the insulin question.

headline: What it actually is
body: Insulin aspart reformulated with niacinamide to speed absorption. A rapid-acting mealtime insulin designed to cover the glucose rise from a meal rather than provide a baseline. | It is monomeric and dimeric rather than zinc-hexameric, which is why it absorbs faster than regular human insulin and why it also crosses the nasal epithelium better, a fact that matters for the intranasal literature.

headline: The axis link
body: Same mechanism as every insulin: portal insulin drives hepatic GH-receptor expression, and *IGFBP-1* falls when insulin is present, which raises **free** IGF-1 rather than total. | The free fraction is the biologically active one. IGFBP-3 in complex with the acid-labile subunit holds roughly **75 to 80%** of circulating IGF-1, and that pool does not move acutely with insulin.
punch: It moves free IGF-1, not total IGF-1.

headline: The preparation matters
body: Not all insulins do this equally. In head-to-head comparison, **protaminated biphasic mixes performed measurably worse** than plain aspart or regular insulin on the IGF-system response. | So within the insulin class there are real differences in how much of this effect you get per unit, and plain rapid-acting preparations sat at the better end.
punch: Plain aspart beat the biphasic mixes.

headline: Glycaemic control is not
body: Four insulin preparations at identical doses produced **parallel decreases in IGFBP-1 despite marked differences in peripheral insulin concentration and plasma glucose**. | The authors concluded that **glycemic response cannot predict IGF-system response**. So you cannot use your glucose meter to tell whether you are getting the effect you are dosing for. There is no accessible feedback signal.
punch: ==You cannot read this effect off a glucose meter.==

headline: The carbohydrate floor
body: Rapid insulin without matching carbohydrate is how hypoglycaemia happens. Covering even a small mealtime dose requires a meaningful carbohydrate load at that meal, every time, without exception or delay. | Which means the compound dictates your eating schedule rather than fitting around it, and a missed or delayed meal becomes a medical event rather than an inconvenience.
punch: It makes every missed meal dangerous.

headline: And glucose blunts GH
body: Here is the conflict nobody puts on the same slide. Glucose-mediated increase in hypothalamic somatostatin is the most plausible explanation for the acute GH suppression after oral glucose, which is the basis of the test used to diagnose acromegaly. | So the carbohydrate you are obliged to eat to use this safely is itself raising somatostatin tone and suppressing GH pulses. The two halves of the protocol work against each other.
punch: _The carbs that make it safe suppress the GH you wanted._

headline: Separate them in time
body: The one thing the evidence does support is not putting a carbohydrate load next to a GH pulse. A pre-bed carbohydrate load flattens the nocturnal slow-wave-sleep GH surge, which is the largest physiological pulse you have. | Protein and arginine are the exception: arginine lowers somatostatin tone and potentiates the GHRH response, which is why the arginine plus GHRH test exists.
punch: Keep carbohydrate away from your largest pulse.

headline: The same missing trial
body: As with every insulin here, the human IGF-1 data comes from insulin-deficient patients having insulin restored. **Free IGF-1 fell below detection in 15 of 17** when it was withdrawn, and rebounded when given back. | That demonstrates the axis needs insulin. It does not demonstrate that extra insulin in someone with a working pancreas moves anything, and that trial has not been run.
punch: Deficiency restored is not surplus added.

headline: Verdict
body: The mechanism is real and better characterised than for most things on this list. The free-versus-total IGF-1 distinction is genuinely useful and almost nobody knows it. | But it has no feedback signal you can read, it forces a carbohydrate schedule that works against GH pulsatility, and the evidence behind it is all from restoring a deficiency. Narrow therapeutic window, no outcome trial.
punch: Real mechanism, no feedback signal, self-conflicting protocol.
